newsitem.title: USA: Edison Calif. hydro runoff seen twice normal.
newsitem.headline: Edison Calif. hydro runoff seen twice normal.

text.p: Spring runoff at Southern California Edison Co's San Joaquin River hydroelectric projects will total 227 percent of normal based on early February snowpack surveys, a company hydrologist said Friday.
At that rate, hydropower would provide 6,500 gigawatt hours (GWh) of Edison's total generation portfolio for calendar 1997, comapred with a long-term average of 4,700 GWh, the hydrologist said.

The generation forecast, however, does not take into account plant outages and other events which might impact hydropower plant operations and remains preliminary with April 1 generally seen as the peak of the snow season.

Precipitation at Edison's central Huntington Lake station in the central Sierra mountains was a record 53.28 inches from October 1996 to January 1997, compared with the previous 43.21 inch record set in 1969, the Edison source said.
The long-term average for the station over the same four-month period is 20.4 inches.
Natural runoff at Edison's Millerton Reservoir was also said to set a new record for October-January at more than 1 million acre feet, compared with 751,000 acre feet in the same 1956 period.
If California precipitation meets normal levels for the rest of the current water year (October 1996-September 1997), it will go down as the state's third wettest year ever, the hydrologist said.
